candidates.original_title: Brain drain: The mere presence of one's own smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity
candidates.description: The 'brain drain' effect found in Ward et al.'s (2017) second experiment, where closer proximity to one's smartphone (on desk) impaired working memory capacity (OSpan performance) compared to other locations, moderated by smartphone reliance.
candidates.citation_sentence: The purpose of the present study was to carry out a direct replication of Ward et al.'s (2017) second experiment.
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly states it is a direct replication, pre-registered on OSF. The main OSpan 'brain drain' effect was not replicated (no significant main effect of smartphone location). The power effect and Go/No-Go null result were replicated. The authors explicitly conclude the 'brain drain' effect was not replicated.

candidates.original_title: Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
candidates.description: The smartphone attachment and dependency inventory has a two-factor structure consisting of smartphone dependence and emotional attachment.
candidates.citation_sentence: The purpose of the present study was to carry out a direct replication of Ward et al.'s (2017) second experiment.
candidates.notes: The replication partially supported Ward et al.'s two-factor findings but produced additional factors, so the outcome is inconclusive.

candidates.original_title: Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
candidates.description: Having one's smartphone closer in proximity, particularly on the desk, reduces working-memory performance on the OSpan task.
candidates.citation_sentence: The purpose of the present study was to carry out a direct replication of Ward et al.'s (2017) second experiment.
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that the main brain-drain effect on OSpan performance failed to replicate. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
